verdict: Equinix grew revenue 11% to $2.57 billion and net income 31% to $489 million, as record bookings and double-digit recurring growth pushed operating profit up 27%.

segments.name: Colocation
segments.note: Renting space, power and cooling in Equinix data centers — the core business.

segments.name: Interconnection
segments.note: Connecting customers to each other, to clouds and to networks inside the same data center.

segments.name: Managed infrastructure
segments.note: Managed services that help customers run their equipment and networks.

segments.name: Other recurring
segments.note: Smaller recurring services outside the three main lines.

segments.name: Non-recurring revenue
segments.note: One-time fees, mainly installation work when a customer moves in.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: The cost of winning and keeping data-center customers.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office: finance, legal, IT and head-office staff.

opex.name: Restructuring and other exit charges
opex.note: One-off costs of realigning teams and exiting activities.

opex.name: Transaction costs
opex.note: Deal costs, mainly for the atNorth joint venture investment.

opex.name: Impairment charges
opex.note: Writing down assets that are worth less than their book value.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $163M, partly offset by $54M of other income (including a non-recurring fee from the atNorth joint venture) and $46M of interest income — a net $63M cost.

takeaways.title: Record bookings
takeaways.text: Annualized gross bookings hit a record $533 million, up 35% year over year, on strong demand and firmer pricing — future recurring revenue stacking up.

takeaways.title: Operating profit jumped
takeaways.text: Operating income rose to $600 million as revenue grew faster than costs; adjusted EBITDA reached $1.32 billion, a 51% margin.

takeaways.title: AFFO per share
takeaways.text: Adjusted funds from operations — the cash-earnings yardstick for REITs — rose 18% per share, helped by a one-time atNorth fee; excluding it, normalized growth was 12%.

oneTimers: A non-recurring fee from Equinix's investment in the atNorth joint venture lifted other income ($54M) and AFFO this quarter; excluding it, AFFO per share grew 12% on a normalized basis.
Operating expenses include $6M of restructuring charges, $20M of transaction costs and $6M of impairment charges.
footerNote: Equinix is a real estate investment trust (REIT). Recurring revenue is rent-like monthly income; AFFO is a non-GAAP REIT measure reconciled in the release. Revenue segments are the worldwide services split from the release's supplemental data.
